summary: This document reviews traditional and improved agroforestry systems in the hot arid regions of India, specifically the Thar desert. It details the ecological and socioeconomic context, the structure of traditional systems, and the benefits of improved agroforestry practices for soil fertility, erosion control, microclimate moderation, and livelihood security.

passages.text: The production and life support system in this part of hot Indian arid zone are constrained by climatic limitations such as low annual precipitation (100–300 mm year-1); very high temperature during summer season (mean maximum temperature 41 C) touching a maximum of 48–50 C.

It was very interesting that yield of pearl millet, main cereal crop of the region, below the canopy of woody components in any system was not affected at all, rather in Ziziphus spp—P. cineraria and Ziziphus spp—P. cineraria—Salvadoran spp systems, it was substantially increased below the tree canopies in comparison of open spaces.

However, legumes such as moth bean, cluster bean, and green gram exhibited slightly yield reduction below the tree canopies, 5.0 % (Ziziphus spp—P. cineraria system) to 19.5 % (P. cineraria system); 12.5 % (Ziziphus spp—P. cineraria—Salvadora spp system) to 18.2 % (Ziziphus spp–P. cineraria system); and 10.0 % (P. cineraria system) to 33.7 % (P. cineraria—A. nilotica system), respectively.

heading_path: Agroforestry Systems Play a Critical Role in Controlling Soil Erosion
passages.text: The shelterbelts on agricultural fields form a type of agroforestry practice which is quite effective in controlling the soil erosion in arid regions. It is clear from the data that the soil loss was higher in agricultural field without trees as compared to field with agroforestry practices (shelterbelts).

heading_path: Agroforestry Systems Provide Economically Viable and Environment Friendly Means to Improve Soil Fertility
passages.text: In general, organic carbon content decreases with depth but the same was slightly higher under the canopy of both the tree species than in open field condition. The total nitrogen, available P and K were higher under the canopy of P. cineraria followed by A. nilotica and the values for the same were lowest in open field condition.

heading_path: Agroforestry Systems Play a Very Important Role in Moderating the Micro-climate in Arid Regions
passages.text: Similarly, it was found during monsoon season that the soil temperature just beneath the tree cover was lower by as much as 16 C in top soil zone and 5 C at 30 cm depth when compared to open field conditions, thereby indicating better soil-thermal regime.
